    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "I will file a harassment complaint…",
      "text": "I will file a harassment complaint against this company if they do not stop contacting me. I have requested this company stop contacting me several times and they have continued to send marketing postal mails approximately once every 10 days. In the fall of 2024, I added my name to the National Do-Not-Call registry and tried other methods to stop all of this unwanted mail. Most mail stopped but BHG letters continued. Approximately 2 months ago, I called again and dedicated some time to having a representative agree to remove all my contact information. They agreed, but said it would take 45 days to remove my name from the list. I thought that was outrageously long, but said \"fine\". They assured me the last mail would arrive on January 16, 2025. I have since received two more mailings from BHG. Finally, I called today and reached a young man named \"Jason\". He said they had complied with my removal request but refused to say how they had complied. I asked for more information but he abruptly hung up on me. Several minutes later, I received text messages from local car dealerships saying that they were responding to my inquiry for a new vehicle. I asked them to verify the source of the inquiry because I suspect it was Jason. They said they would look into this. More to follow there. A BBB complaint will follow, and I am considering a harassment charge in the local FL district court. Good luck, Jason.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

    {
      "stars": 2,
      "title": "Transparency Needed for a Better Loan Experience",
      "text": "I recently applied for a personal loan through BHG Financial. While the initial experience with the sales representative was positive, the process became frustrating later on. Despite providing all required documents promptly, my application was ultimately denied because a Green Card or U.S. Citizenship was required—information that was not disclosed during the pre-approval process or initial discussions.\n\nEven with a strong credit score of around 740 and a co-borrower, I was offered an interest rate of 21.45% for an 84-month term on a $187,000 loan, with a 5% origination fee. These terms were higher than I expected based on my credit profile and the market.\n\nI would encourage BHG Financial to improve transparency during the pre-approval process and provide more competitive terms for customers with strong credit. While the sales team was helpful at the start, the overall experience fell short of my expectations.\n\nEnded up getting loan from different lender with much better terms. Savings of 11k and around 13% interest rate.",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "The absolute worst experience I've ever…",
      "text": "The absolute worst experience I've ever had. You hear about predatory loan companies and also abusive ones like this company. Bhg demanded a whole bunch of information from me multiple times in a row and wasted my time only to give me an ambiguous reason as to why they rejected my application. I was given a number to call to inquire about the specifics and when I called that number they said that it's a separate department and that nobody can provide that information that it's private. Sort of like all of the personal data which I shared with these loan sharks. Fortunately I was able to easily get a loan with my excellent credit from another provider at it rate that's amazing.     {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Bad experience for business loan",
      "text": "I engaged this company for small business funding. They kept selling the fact that they don't report the loan on your credit. Their rates and fees are on the high side, and it seemed they were using this selling point as a way to justify it.\n\nWell, turns out they still put a UCC lien on your business, so it has the same affect as being reported on credit. And if you ask to pay off your loan early, they will ask for 5 years of payments.\n\nAlso, they initially told me I had to buy very expensive \"loan insurance\", and only after I said I was not interested, they then said it was optional insurance.\n\nVery shady company in my opinion and I will not do business with them again.\n\nEdit: to reply to their response.\nYes, someone did reach out. They couldn't guarantee anything and said it was unlikely, but said they could \"try\".\n\nYes, the terms were clear. But the lien is not disclosed (they aren't required to). The sales reps know what they are doing.\n\nThe loan is fine, but they will not see anymore of my business in the future. Especially after this fluff response.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2024-09-16T14:06:38.000Z",

    {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "Diamond ring or medical deductible?",
      "text": "The entire team at BHG have been phenomenal since I initially submitted my application. Rick, Angie and the rest of the support team have created a loyal customer for the rest of my life. They were able to clearly communicate all of the next steps, follow up via personalized emails, Easy to reply text messages as well as the very intimate personal phone call. As a seasoned sales professional for 20 years, I was blown away by this support attention to detail and dedication to the customer experience.\nMy particular situation included a very large healthcare, coupled with the desire to make a large purchase in the form of engagement ring. Having to choose between a very large deductible payment or a diamond ring is not something that is very easy; your health or the love of your life?\nThese human beings were able to understand that this was a very difficult time and decision and expedited my application with due diligence, professionalism, and attention to detail within the fiduciary world, and all of the responsibilities and laws that are built out to protect us all.\nI am forever grateful for human touch and making me feel like more than just a name on an application and a number.     {
      "stars": 2,
      "title": "Lacks Basic Client Transparency & Tools",
      "text": "BHG offers straightforward and quick financing options, but the experience comes with significant drawbacks. While the rates are notably higher than other financial institutions, the appeal of non-agency reporting may seem like a fair trade-off—until you experience their subpar customer service.\n\nIf you're used to the convenience of an online portal to manage your account—whether it's checking your principal balance, changing payment methods, or making basic updates like an address change—prepare to be disappointed. BHG lacks even the most rudimentary online customer portal, as confirmed by their own customer service team. This means there's no way to manage your account electronically in real-time.\n\nAdding to the frustration, they don’t provide standard monthly statements, whether electronically or by mail, even if you request them. The best they can offer is an amortization schedule, which is hardly a substitute. When you're borrowing between $100,000 to $500,000, the absence of basic self-service tools or at least a monthly statement is unacceptable. Transparency and ease of account management are fundamental expectations in today's financial landscape, and BHG falls short on both fronts.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2024-08-17T00:58:14.000Z",

    {
      "stars": 3,
      "title": "Loan request",
      "text": "It wasn’t the easiest process I’ve been through I’ve started this process on 6/5 and it’s now 6/21. Initially I was told I qualified for a 10 year loan and should qualify for $166,000 but when the paperwork it said 7 years $111,000. I was also told initially told the loan should be through underwriting by the end of the day on 6/7, I provided everything I was asked to provide, then it was something else I needed to provide time and time again. This entire process I never received a call from anyone I had to call the main line and had to be transferred to whom ever at that point was working on my loan. In 6/20 I called around 3:30 est since I haven’t heard from anyone if everything was good because I was to be funded on Monday 6/24 I had to explain a loan on April 4 and a check on April 8th and was told she had a meeting at 4pm est and she would call me back immediately after and she never did so I called today 6/21 and was told she was gone for the day so I requested to talk to her manager but Tori called me just to inform me everything is good and will be funded on Monday.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

    {
      "stars": 4,
      "title": "Decently Pleasant Experience",
      "text": "The Team of professionals at BHG made the experience a pleasant one. Knowing that I am agreeing to pay heavily for immediate funds is sort of calming but necessary. Understanding the lending business is absolutely paramount prior to committing to an agreement. Do your research and be prepared to know that 20+% is the going rate in 2024. And tack that on to each years amount left. Going the full term of the loan could result in paying double what you borrowed. Truth in the details. This was a means to a better daily process and I don’t regret it yet. I appreciate the team’s dedication in following up and offering explanations to all my concerns. S/O: Alison, Hannah, Brittani, and Angie for your pleasant customer service!",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",

    {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "My experience with BHG was very positive",
      "text": "My experience with BHG was very positive. From the initial interview, to financing my money. The process is very transparent, and they explained how the soft credit pull worked. My only complaint is that BHG has no online site where you can track your repayment progress, schedule your payments, or even pay additional payments to pay off your loan sooner.     {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "Business loan",
      "text": "Business loan. My interaction with BHG started with a flyer in the mail. Intrigued, I filled out a short questionnaire online & was then contacted by TJ, a BHG associate. He was very professional and explained the services they offered in great detail. I decided to move forward with the application based on it all being from a soft credit pull. I did not want any new inquiries on my personal credit right now, so that definitely helped to see what kind of an offer I would receive. After selecting a product, I was handed off to Jessica who was very personable and knowledgeable. She gave me a few days to consider the offer & we closed on Monday. My experience with BHG concluded with Angie, who was also incredibly helpful. After the details were finalized, Angie assured I would receive a wire that day. Everyone I spoke to was very friendly & I would definitely recommend them to other small businesses seeking funding options either for an established business, or start-up. Overall, great dealing with them.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Don't use these people, borrowers beware...",
      "text": "I purchased a puppy using their Nalupay umbrella of financing. These people financed $2,700 for 72 months. I've had the loan for a year and 20+ payments and the balance has not moved. When I make payments two days before \"the new cycle\" they say it goes to the principal and I still owe another payment. Then if you need to wait to make another payment they relentlessly call you after you should technically be ahead a payment. They provide no information saying that if you pay slightly outside of what they consider to be the cycle by a day that they will consider that a principle payment. They also don't tell you how predatory they are. I love my dog but will never do anything with Nalupay again. I want to lump sum this payment but I'm afraid they won't give me a payoff amount. Customer service is beyond rude. 1 star all day long. I have all of the payment info, and totally welcome someone to contact me and tell me why this is the way they operate. Everyone that I've spoken with has not wanted to take 2 seconds to really look at the account. If I see a response here, I will be monitoring and update/edit this post with a response. If I have to I will also post all my payment info. My account is current and I have nothing to hide. It seems like BHG/Nalupay does though.\n\nUpdate ...2/19/24\nSomeone did in fact reach out and was very nice. But everything I stated above is accurate. I am locked into a loan for 72 months and reviewing the account with an agent, confirmed I've paid over $1,100 on the loan and only around $200 went to principal. The loan balance started at $2500 and is now $2200. I am working to identify a balance transfer product that works for this loan. But I would strongly advise against a loan with them unless completely necessary.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2024-02-19T22:55:33.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {
        "verified": false,

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Biggest Mistake of my Life",
      "text": "Very nice representatives and easy to get funded but I did not realize the first 100 months is all interest and nothing towards principle making this loan very preditory. It cost me $37,409.76 to borrow $100,000 with my 24 month commitment. I called yesterday to tell them to please not charge me the last $1,558.74 monthy fee because it was the 1st and I was trying to pay it back in full the same day monthly (all interest fee) was taken. The representative said that is not an option and took another $1,558.74 just because they could with no remourse. I have never felt so violated.",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Gatekeepers win again",
      "text": "If you got denied once and you keep getting emails saying that “we revisited your file and you might now be eligible for financing”. Don’t waste your time! This was a complete waste of energy and hope. At the end of the day they have “good” words pretending like they care but they are not here to help us be financially free. If you’re looking for 20k loan with 28.99% apr BHG Money is a GREAT option and you will have a chance. And let’s be honest with ourselves, we all know who those type of loans are for. Honestly, if you have a goal of being financially free don’t look to BHG money to help you. They are what I like to call a “GATEKEEPER”. They know what money can do for you. Giving you a loan goes against their agenda of widening the gap between poor and rich.\nAnd lastly, to my peeps, I know you are all waking up to the reality of how this world functions. A word to the wise, continue opening your eyes so that you can be cognizant of businesses like BHG money who are only here to make money off of you.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

      "stars": 1,
      "title": "DO NOT ACCEPT BHG LOANS! They're flawed!",
      "text": "BHG IS A TOTAL SCAM!!!! Sure, they are willing to help you obtain the funds you need fast, but AT A RIP OFF, COMPLETELY AND LEGAL STEAL from the borrower's hard-earned money. Please read carefully everything and make sure you ask every question possible before you sign-up. I'm living hell now trying to deal with them.\n\nWhat started as a dream for business venture has turned out to be a complete headache and most of all heartache! I started my business, but sadly my original $50K loan has a \"hold\" and I'm unable to pay it off before the 48th month commitment they NEVER explained to me. In the end, I will end-up paying these thieves DOUBLE of the original amount ($93,408)\n\nThey charged me $3,000 origination fee, which dropped my funded amount to $47,000 in January 2022. Two years into the loan (now 2024), I've made 24 payments of $1112. However, over $16,000 has been only for interest and according to their loan amortization as of January 2024 I still owe $47,000 on the loan. A RIP OFF!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!\n\nDO NOT GET THEIR LOANS! I totally regret getting myself into this rip off loan and there is nothing I can do about it except warn you all that THEY'RE THE ABSOLUTE WORST!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!\n\nDO NOT, DO NOT , DO NOT LEND FROM BHG!\n\nTheir only reply and argument is \"BHG uses simple interest, fixed rate loans. Much like a mortgage or auto loan, the interest is calculated against your loan’s outstanding balance. As time goes on and you start paying down your principal, the amount of interest paid each month decreases\". However, a consumer CAN'T pay off the principal before a certain hold they get on you. In the end, doesn't matter if the interest is \"low\" as they claim; when a consumer IS NOT ABLE to pay down the principal because of a hold we still end up paying outrageous amounts of interest fees (thus cheating the hardworking people).\n\nYes, they contacted me, but now their deal is just as bad as the original loan itself.       "stars": 1,
      "title": "A follow up to my review",
      "text": "Besides ruining my week and causing me a lot of undue stress by not getting back to me after numerous emails, texts and phone calls - after having me sign and send a signed 8821 form that allows the IRS to share all of my information with them (which no one asks for) and leading me to believe I had been scammed, the least BHG can do it pay me back for the Life Lock subscription I had to purchase for $300, the notary fees $15 to notarize a letter to the IRS to rescind the 8821 form I signed for them, and the postal certified mail fees of $7.50 to send it to the IRS. I also had to spend the time to freeze all of my credit accounts.     {
      "stars": 4,
      "title": "Quality People…Confusing Process",
      "text": "The individuals I dealt with were very professional and respectful of my time. I appreciated being able to conduct most exchanges online for my personal loan. I ultimately selected BHG because they will not report the loan to the credit bureaus unless I default. The BHG review process has many “transparent to customer” handoffs and steps between departments that had me resubmitting documents 2 & 3 times, which was confusing & frustrating. I talked with no less than 7 people in different departments - after the 3rd dept, after I was given notice of approval and e-signed my docs, I still had 3 other gauntlets to pass to release funds. The review was painfully in depth, with proof of direct deposit, 2 months of paystubs, demand for 3+ months of bank statements for all direct deposit accounts and requiring I give them access to 10 years of my tax returns, it felt surprisingly invasive for a soft-credit pull, but in the end, I got a reasonable rate and term that made it worth my time.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-11-28T19:03:47.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {

        "useful_votes": 0,

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "BEWARE!!!!!",
      "text": "BEWARE!!!!!\nI received a loan very quickly as I have 800 credit score and earn 250k per year. I was SHOCKED when I saw the amortization schedule, that I had to ASK for because they do not provide any type of statements nor do they have an on line portal. I took out a $45k dollar loan and the amount of interest I am being charged for the entire loan (if I kept it for the 5 years) is $40,428.76! Almost 100% of the loan amount! I dont even know if this is legal. I have an excellent credit score! Needless to say I am paying off the loan. I got a loan for the exact same amount, within ONE day from American Express and in 5 years I will pay $6,598 interest! That is a far cry for $40,428.76! Never in the process of getting this loan from BHG did someone tell me or show me how much interest I would be paying. DO NOT DO BUSINESS WITH THIS COMPANY. Hopefully they will allow this review on their website.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Don't fall for the marketing",
      "text": "I'll admit the grand marketing from this company got me on board, and it not showing up on my credit report was an added draw. I opted to not take the full amount it was approved for because of the large monthly payments, but over the first year I received multiple e-mails from Leonardo and Karen informing me that I was originally approved for more and I should definitely take it based on my original approval and my consistent payment status. I also had a phone call with Karen about it and she made me feel like I was an idiot to decline. I finally decided to go ahead and take it after being harassed for a year, and then was declined. I felt so deceived. Fast forward to now and I did miss 1 payment that I am rescheduling due to unforeseen circumstances and I have gotten an unbelievable amount of emails, text messages and phone calls from Stephanie. None of which are like, \"hey, you never miss a payment, is everything ok?\" no - it's all - hey you missed a payment we need to reschedule it. Starting only 6 days after the missed payment. Make no mistake, this is a business of course, but the marketing people pretend to care about you, once you're in, you are not a human anymore, you are just a number.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-10-19T03:04:39.000Z",
        "experience": ""

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "APPLICATION REJECTED BEFORE SUBMISSION",
      "text": "My credit score is 790. I applied for a loan and while on the phone with the account executive, I received an email that my application had been rejected. Mind you, this was before I even submitted my paycheck (paystubs) to qualify me.\n\nSo by only checking my credit which was high and not even undergoing a review of my income, I get an email by the system that my incomplete application had been rejected.\n\nThe AE couldn’t explain why I received a rejection letter while I was on the phone with her, as she informed me it should have taken an hour and she didn’t even receive my paystub yet.\n\nI proceeded to call the company and speak with management to find out what happened but they all avoided me and the conversation. I’m black and have no bankruptcy, no default loans on my credit cards. Nothing at all.\n\nThe fact that the system rejected my application even before I finished my submission is very concerning.\n\nEveryone gets to submit a full application as it’s the fair thing to do but I get rejected while entering the details of my application?\n\nKudos to the many of you who claim you had a better experience. I won’t challenge the veracity in your experience.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-10-04T23:15:57.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {
        "verified": false,
        "useful_votes": 0,
        "page_number": 52,
        "source_url": "https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bhgfinancial.com?page=52"
      }
    },

      "text": "This is by far the worst experience I've ever had with not just a lending company, but a company in general. I recently funded a note with this company where I was approved for $110,000. Started with $50k and 30 days later came back to draw on the remaining amount. When I went to apply and log into my portal it said welcome Rafael. That is not my name which caused a system error that no one has been able to explain why that happened. That took over a week. The we restarted the application and they asked to confirm my email on file and it was for a Dante. Finally get the docs and am told the funding team will be reaching out. Four hours ago go by and my funding coordinator sends me a stip list and will not return my calls for over three days as one of the stips was an account ending in four numbers I was not familiar with. Then a sales manager called and when I asked what account that was he had no idea either. Finally downloaded my paystub and the account they requested was my HSA account thinking it was a bank statement. Then after receving all stips I'm told I was declined. No one can tell me why, but that I will receive a letter in the mail in 7-10 business days explaining the decline. Stay as far away from this company as possible.\n\nYou can see from their response after all this no one on the team has explained why this was declined. Just passed me off and I’ll get a letter in 7-10 business days explaining the decline. This review should show anyone working with this company the type of service you will get.",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Complete waste of time!!!!!",
      "text": "I applied through BHG and made sure I sent everything they asked for immediately. Account executive said everything looked great and he seen no problem with any of my information. After waiting a week and not hearing anything I reached out to them to find out when and if I was going to hear anything. Within a couple of hours I heard from them saying it was with the underwriter in a final review awhile later they reached back out now after me waiting a week they wanted more information. They sent me a form that would not allow me to edit, print or anything so no way of appeasing this new requirement so, I told them to forget it and cancel my application. I received a letter in the mail 2 weeks later telling me they denied me because I did not meet the requirements. Funny, not only do I have a credit score around 800 but, when I applied at another lender I had an approval within 5 minutes. Even funnier I kept getting their mailers for about 3 weeks until I finally called them and told them to stop. Trust me it's not worth wasting your time applying I am still at a loss as to why after waiting a week they couldn't tell me anything but yet came back asking for more information that if truly needed should have been asked for long before.\nUpdate 9/29/2023 After receiving the auto response from BHG I will add this the document that was sent to me was NOT a Docu-sign document it would not allow any actions on my part so nice try. I still stand firm on not recommending BHG Money to anyone. Read the reviews and also the auto replies that they always use. I have almost perfect credit and have a 100% on time payment record I have never been turned down for any loans until BHG sent me a denial after I said I was done this after waiting a week and still not knowing what the status on my application was.",

    {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "First Time Customer",
      "text": "I am pleased with this process and company so far. The lending amounts are much higher than most with unmatched benefits and comparable rates. Everyone I spoke to was pleasant and I appreciated the quick turnaround and thorough walk through the application process. The whole process for me took about a week and half. I did have plenty of questions and wanted to see multiple options, which were answered and provided without hassle. I would have liked to have been given notice that I would be working with a team and was provided their contact information at the beginning. I had contact with at least four people, again all pleasant and knowledgeable. I understand the online portal is new or at least a work in progress. It was cumbersome going back and forth between emails, online portal and text/calls to collective information and to submit sensitive documents. In the end everything got to where it needed to go. Again, I am pleased with the process and company and looking forward to working with this team for the length of our loan and possibly after. Thank you to the team for a quick and mostly painless experience!",

    {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "Best debt consolidation loan experience",
      "text": "I had many offers for a consolidation loan, and I chose this company based off the reviews of credit karma. The loan rep (Ricardo) was very kind, not pushy, and ended up having to run numbers 3 different times for me as I wanted to make the best decision. He was responsive, clear on expectations, and the salesforce portal was easy to use. I had an issue uploading the required documents and it was very easy to accommodate/ provided back up routes to upload. I have done a consolidated loan prior, and the steps this company takes to verify identification are amazing and the more thorough steps I have experienced. It was also easy to reach out via email, text and phone. I also loved the No early payoff penalties. I do not remember the lady I spoke to when I first called in before she connected me with the sales team, but she was so kind, and so was michael who was very prompt and clear on expectations! 10/10",
      "company_response": "",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Very unprofessional experience",
      "text": "We were told we were approved for $190k, all that was needed was a pay slip and picture of ID. We provided this and we were told funds were cleared, but we never got the paper work. We called for updates and were told we needed to provide pictures of our house and another selfie - for a business loan. Seemed very sketchy, so we said we would just not move forward. We were asked by Richard to reconsider, so we did, against our better judgement sent the other pictures in and…nothing. We asked for an update and we’re told we were denied. This with an over 800 credit score and well over $200k in income, and we only wanted $50k of the $190 approved. We even signed the documents agreeing to the terms! When asked why, we were told no one was allowed to tell us and there was no one we could speak to outside of Richard, the person who was unable to explain why we were approved, looking to release funds, and then suddenly denied out of nowhere. The other people we had dealt with during the process, Michael and Allen, never responded at all to our questions through the process. I would highly recommend going with another lending company. We have never been turned down before and there is no legitimate reason we should have been turned down this time, either. We were told by another bank we will work with that BHG is notoriously difficult and we weren’t the first horror story. Just go elsewhere and don’t waste your time. We weren’t a difficult or complicated situation, so if they can’t get us through, there is something very wrong with this organization.\n\nUPDATE: I received the adverse letter and it states “unable to to verify applicant information” which is amazingly vague and very difficult to believe after sending in 2 selfies, 2 pictures of ID front and back, a picture of the outside of our house and inside of our house and a payslip. Comically, in the same mail, we got a “VIP” invitation to apply for money from BHG. Again, run from this outfit. We have been approved for a much larger loan with far less issue. I will post who with in a separate post for those seeking a professional experience.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-08-10T19:01:14.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {

        "useful_votes": 0,
        "page_number": 72,
        "source_url": "https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bhgfinancial.com?page=72"
      }
    },

    {
      "stars": 2,
      "title": "Be careful of the marketing",
      "text": "I approached BHG for a loan to cover IVF and surrogacy expenses. (They had sent me in the mail glossy loan offers on a weekly basis for several months, so I finally decided see what they would offer me.) My FICO score is above 800. it was 850 a few months ago. I've never had a missed payment on anything and represent very low credit risk.\n\nThe BHG loan offer had an origination rate of 3.5% and an interest rate of %17.49 (APR of 18.45%). I found these rates very high. The person I spoke to tried to convince me to get a loan (there was a salesman quality to it) and was encouraging me to take even longer-term (e.g. 10 year) vs. a 3 year loans saying I could prepay anytime I wanted so the term didn't matter.\n\nNot true. First, I didn't need a 10-year loan. Second, he failed to mention that when you take longer-term loans, you pay way more interest even if you prepay. So If you take a 10 year loan and pay if off in 2 years, you will have paid a lot of interest and still owe most of the loan whereas taking a 3 year loan and paying it off in 2 years, by the time you pay it off you will have reduced the amount you owe substantially. (Look it up. This is how self- amortizing loans, like mortgage loans, work.) I found his trying to market a long-term, high-interest loan, with origination fee too, when I didn't need a 10-year loan, together with his omission of the costliness of the long-term loans, somewhat unethical. I passed on the offer.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-07-26T14:28:54.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {
        "verified": false,
        "useful_votes": 0,
        "page_number": 73,
        "source_url": "https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bhgfinancial.com?page=73"

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "BHG’s pre approved solicitation is…",
      "text": "BHG’s pre approved solicitation is typical of companies that appear to be “Helpful Lenders”. As is the case of 99% the only will make a loan if you first prove “You do not need the money.” In our case it was strictly to combine our debts of which we have never been late on the payments. If they had been a truthful lender the loan would have reduced our monthly payments by over $600.00 increasing our discretionary income. That scenario would have allowed us to pay off our debts faster. Logic and common sense do not exist.\nThe response I received from BHG was not an answer to my concerns, just a company policy statement. The only way to get a loan in this environment is to prove you do not need the money regardless of your proven history of paying you bills on time.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-07-24T18:29:16.000Z",

    {
      "stars": 5,

    {
      "stars": 3,
      "title": "Too Good To Be True? Perhaps.",
      "text": "My caution to anyone taking out a BHG loan is to really study the amortization schedule and interest rate for your loan before committing. DO YOUR HOMEWORK CAREFULLY.\n\nAt the time of our loan, we were in a cash flow crisis, so our focus was on quick cash availability. When we got back on our feet, I reached about repayment only to find that although we had paid about $42k on the approximate $105k we borrowed, only about $11k was principle and the rest - a whopping $31k - was interest. Our payoff amount after 30 monthly payments of $1,392 was only 11k less than the original loan!\n\nYou'd think that the interest to principle rate would be apparent month to month, but BHG has no loan portal and you don't get monthly statements, so unless you pin the amortization schedule to your fridge, you are likely to forget once you get the loan.\n\nI understand the benefits that BHG offers (which I'm sure will be reiterated in a BHG response), but know that you might be paying a HUGE long term price for your \"quick\" money. Money from BHG was some of the most expensive money I have ever borrowed. If I could go back and erase the experience, I would.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-07-09T00:14:04.000Z",
        "experience": ""

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Spoke to a rep over 2 years ago bc I…",
      "text": "Spoke to a rep over 2 years ago bc I kept receiving very large and sometimes heavy envelopes making it look like it was a personal letter (important docs). The loan was not a good fit for me or our business so I told the rep I wasn’t interested. But I still keep receiving these large legal sized envelopes -now - not just through the U.S. post office but UPS. I’ve even called several times and asked to be removed. I was assured I was. They won’t stop! Imagine someone knocking on your door twice a week and making it sound like an urgent matter to tend to. So I open it bc it looks like official business docs with only return address no name of company. It feels like Stalking or harassment. Even though its mail, it feels like it. I’ve even marked them “please return to sender!” But they’re in my mailbox twice a week. Company must have serious money from the interest rates to waste it like this. It’s very costly paper and printing that gets trashed.\nTrying to upload photos but not able.",

      "title": "Objectively one of the best out there..",
      "text": "Although I decided against the options presented for potential funding opportunities, BHG has been such a pleasure to work with!\n\nIf you’re like me and are new to the concept of business credit, you should most definitely consider working with them. I will say that it’s very hard to find lenders these days that are as straightforward as BHG. Even my local bank that has been handling finances per my personal and business accounts for years couldn’t facilitate an easy application process comparable to BHG.\n\nWith less emphasis on personal credit history, quick turnaround times, and dedicated customer service, this organization is easily one of the best out there.     {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "I’ve called twice since this they say they’ll return my call no one calls.",
      "text": "BHG loan is good but DO NOT let them talk you into their credit card ! I had a 790 credit score and let them talk me into a credit card when I got a personal loan. I agreed as they said they had negative impact on my credit score and it would help build up my credit score . Unfortunately, my car was broken into (I have a police report) and my cards , license and social security cards were stolen while I was on a nursing travel assignment. I reported all of my cards stolen and shared my police report. Within 3 hours the Thieves charged over 8k on my cards all over Indianapolis . I immediately called creditors and all were corrected . I called bhg and reported and they said over 2k had been charged but they would close out the account and report the theft. They said they would send a new new card out .I never received a new one in the mail . I honestly forgot about the card because I never use it. A year later, a delinquent payment is being reported on my credit score. I was immediately scared as I knew it wasn’t right. It is from this card ! I called to find out the error and I was told the card now had a yearly fee and was delinquent on that fee. I explained the card was stolen , charges had been made fraudulent and I reported it long ago, Hence the reason why they had me down for a second card .I have not been late on my loans with them so I know they know I’m not trying to get out of paying . I’ve called twice in the past 2 months and both agents are telling me the same thing that they can see that I called for a second card but whoever I spoke to did not write a note . So the first person told me the fraudulent charges were washed out due to the fraud but that they were going to see what they could do to get the fee waived and fix the credit report .I was told I’d get a call back but I did not .\n\nIt still is being reported that I’m delinquent so I called again and went through the whole thing with a Second Lady and now she is telling me I owe over 2 k in charges because they can’t find notes from my calls! Before this I had a perfect credit payment and now I’m showing 90 days delinquent on a card I’ve never used and I’m irate !!! I didn’t work this hard to have my credit ruined over a stolen card. Amex and Sam’s were stolen too and I did not have a problem at all with them . I’ll never recommend an apex card! I mean how hard is it to admit someone forgot to write a note because obviously I called if a new one was sent out . And if I never used the card and have not been late on my loan payments, why not waive the card fee since I didn’t even have it in my possession or use it ? Common sense not good business .",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },

        "experience": ""

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "DO NOT get any loan with this Predatory…",
      "text": "DO NOT get any loan with this Predatory lender! Will loan large amounts of money with high interest rates, then lock you in for a period which you can not refinance or payoff early. During that time you are ONLY PAYING THE INTEREST. In the end you’ll have paid more than double what you borrowed. They tell you they will provide an end of the year statement so the “interest paid can be written off” Its a LIE they don’t! Communication is great while going through the loan process however, once they have dispersed the funds….crickets! STAY FAR AWAY. There are other options if you’re trying to get a business loan.",
      "company_response": "",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "I applied for a loan with BHG about a real estate aquisition.",
      "text": "I applied for a loan with BHG about a year ago. I have a small business and was exploring funding options for real estate acquisition. They informed me they could not approve my loan at this time. Ok, no problem. I have many funding avenues and a credit score over 800.\n\nThe problems started a few months ago. A rep from BHG called me and said that they could now approve my loan, they were now using new criteria for underwriting on real estate transactions. I have received 17 mailings, most full size expensive cardboard pieces, so I thought this must be legitimate and they are trying to increase their loan portfolio.\n\nLast week I followed the instruction on one of the mailers, and filled out an application again to acquire a few single family homes for short term rentals. No one responded for a week, then I got a call from someone who said I filled out a calculator and wanted to follow up. Seems the person who had the application just never followed up on it.\n\nTwo hours later he calls back, and just says they are not able to proceed with my application. BHG, no worries, I don't really need the loan or your money, but what I don't appreciate is pre-qualified literature sent to my home, 17 times, and wasting my time filling out applications.\n\nYour lending business just wastes so much marketing and the stories your loan officers tell are just not truthful. I guess you fooled me twice... but never again. I will campaign against your brand. I would not have been sour with one denial, or that I don't fit your program criteria.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-03-28T22:45:25.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {

        "useful_votes": 0,
        "page_number": 93,
        "source_url": "https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bhgfinancial.com?page=93"
      }

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "BHG is Horrible, STAY AWAY",
      "text": "This is a horrible company. I was sent a mailer with a QR code indicating I was pre-approved for a loan. Out of curiosity and needing a debt consolidation loan, I scanned the code. I was contacted the next day via text by a representative by the name of Dominic asking what I was looking for in a loan. I ignored the text. A coupe days later I received a phone call from Dominic. He appeared to be professional and was pleasant to talk to. I explained to him that I was potentially looking for a loan to consolidate credit card debt. I agreed to provide him with my personal information in order to run a soft credit inquiry. Dominic then went over my credit information and indicated that he would send an email to me requesting my pension reward letter and income tax returns. I hung up with the impression that I was dealing with a professional and BHG would be a good company to deal with. Boy was I wrong! I never received an email and I have attempted to contact Dominic several times via text and VM to no avail. Now I am worried that my personal information may be used fraudulently by BHG. Do yourself a favor a stay way clear of this classless and unprofessional organization. Extremely poor customer service. I plan to investigate my legal options as this company has taken my personal information and have not contacted me. BHG cannot be trusted and please stay away from them.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

      "date": {
        "published": "2023-03-11T03:35:24.000Z",
        "experience": ""

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Existing customer with a terrible experience",
      "text": "I was an existing customer with a 790 credit score and automated monthly payments that were always timely. Following my 3 year term requirement, I received an email from a representative stating I qualified for a lower interest rate on my existing loan. I filled out the requested documents and waited patiently for a response, which never came. I reached out via email and a representative stated I didn’t qualify for a lower interest rate and said I’d be getting a letter in the mail explaining the decision, which also never came. I just paid off the loan to it’s entirety and will NEVER work with this company again. As a customer of BHG for nearly 4 years, I highly recommend taking your business elsewhere.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "False advertising and predatory lending practices",
      "text": "Only reason I opened this credit account was because I was promised if I balance transfered in the first 60 days I would get 0% interest on the transfer. So I got my credit ran and signed up. I did the balance transfer and 6 days past and I didn't see the balance transfer on my account. When I asked I was told it takes 15 business days. After 15 business days, nothing still. When I asked, they said maybe 20 business days. After 23 business days still nothing. When I asked, finally they looked into it and realized something went wrong. They canceled the payment then said my 60 day window has now closed and I don't qualify for the 0% balance transfer. They blame it on the bank, that bank blames in on the other bank and the only one who gets screwed is me, the consumer, who did nothing wrong. I asked if they could request a special acception based on the information showing I did nothing wrong, of course it was denied. I'm in the middle of a major project and needed these funds available which is the only reason I let them run my credit to open this account and now the funds are unavailable and they just say \"hey, sorry about that buddy, we know its not your fault but nothing we can do\" and wash thier hands of the situation. Why weren't they on top of this from the beginning? When someone is transferring $17k to an account with you, why is nobody making sure that money actually arrives? Why am I the one calling constantly to have them check up on their job? Why was the issue not caught by them instead of me having to contact them 3 times before they realized it was an issue? Now they say they'll put in a second request for me but that takes about 30 days to get a response. Yeah, my project will be over by then so thanks for nothing. I'm sure companies like this do this type of predatory practice constantly. Sell you the idea of zero interest balance transfer then drag along the transfer until after the 60 day mark. Now you're credit has been ran and they hope you'll start charging on the card with full interest. Shameful",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2023-02-16T00:36:31.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {
        "verified": false,
        "useful_votes": 0,
        "page_number": 99,
        "source_url": "https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bhgfinancial.com?page=99"
      }

    {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "Great Experience Guided by True Professionals",
      "text": "Anthony Felicia and Nick Marji are both tremendous to work with. Anthony handled the initial inquiry and helped not only answer questions, but also made sure we had the necessary information completed. Once we were approved, Anthony walked us through the next steps and provided a timeline of when to expect a follow up call from Nick. Anthony kept us updated as he was working with Anthony to establish the time for the follow up call.\nThe handoff from Anthony to Nick was seamless. We initially expected to have the call with Nick on the following morning, but Anthony and Nick made it work to have it on the afternoon of the day we were notified of our approval. Nick was outstanding in sharing the steps required to complete the funding process. Usually having to go through a laundry list of items is less than exciting, but Nick provided the overview in a way that was informative and engaging. While I am sure his list of calls is full, Nick made it seem as if we were his only applicants for the day. After walking through the steps needed to be completed, Nick followed up with an e-mail recapping our conversation and made sure we had his cell number and e-mail to be able to text/e-mail any questions. Both appreciative of and impressed with the attention to detail exhibited by Anthony and Nick. Each said what he was going to do and then did what he said he was going to do. Couldn't ask for two better individuals to work with.",
      "company_response": "",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "I can’t believe I ignored reviews",
      "text": "I can’t believe I ignored the bad reviews. They all say the same thing about giving personal information and then never hearing back. I brought this up in my call and was told it only takes 1min to fill out the preliminary application online or 5 minutes on the phone. So I did. Then never heard back. I hate this. I’m usually better than this at gauging what’s safe and what’s not. If you’re reading this, good on you for searching for reviews. Now steer clear. Go elsewhere.\n\n*EDIT*\nBHG requested more information or else this review could be taken down. So here it is. I got multiple offers in the mail. I scanned the QR acode for an offer and was prompted to enter information. That drew me away so I thought I wouldn’t hear back from them. Then a few days later I got a text message from someone asking if I’m still interested. It turns out you don’t even need to fill out the info, they get notified anyway after you scan the QR code. I didn’t think anything of the texts since I was already thinking I’m not interested. Anyway, I engaged with and ended up talking on the phone with the sales rep. His name is Dan Camp. He graciously answered all my questions and was very reasonable with explanations even when I expressed my concern that Trustpilot shows many low ratings are due to not hearing back after providing information. That’s exactly what happened to me. I called customer service and turns out I was declined. Why not even have the decency to tell me via text or email if they already have the information. Even if BBB provides a high grade of this business, it’s the least that can be done to provide instant information once the request is declined. Sure we’ll get notification in snail mail about the details why declined but why let us wait in agony thinking we made a mistake and fell for a scam. If it’s not a scam, then be better and contact immediately. When I called, I was told the mail will come in 30 days. That could have easily been provided in a text or email. They only treat you well if they get your business. If not, you’re not worth their time. An A+ business would not discriminate in this fashion. In fact, the only reason why they provide the reason for declining (in the mail and no other form) is probably because it’s required by law. Ghosting all other platforms on the other hand is completely allowed. Shady business. If relationships matter to you and you’re not sure if you’ll get approved or not, then don’t bother with these people. Unless they change their methods. I truly hope they improve cuz they obvi have helped many others. Although I do question the 5-star ratings on here. The 2-, 3-, and 4-star ones seem legit. The 5-star ones don’t provide enough detail yet those ones don’t get threatened to be taken down when not enough details are provided, so for all we know, they could be fake! See, shady.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "BHG to Potential Customers: Don't Bother Us",
      "text": "After applying on my own, I was informed five days later that I would need a co-borrower. I asked if this was due to income or credit rating reasons, and was told the rep is not given that kind of information. So I guessed as to who might be best as a co-borrower and they gave their information. It has been 6 days since then and the rep will not answer my calls or return text messages and emails asking for a status. I intuited this meant I was not approved, although I was clueless as to why. Eventually I tracked down an 800 number and the helpful lady on the other end informed me I was not approved and would receive a letter. I suppose this is their rep's immature way of avoiding hard conversations with potential borrowers. Had I been given the courtesy of knowing what I was lacking, I could have worked with another co-borrower who had a stronger application. Word of warning to potential borrowers, don't waste your time unless you are *positive* you will qualify. Their online estimator is not at all accurate, and if you do not qualify initially they will provide no insight as to why - they will just ask for more and then ghost you like a teenager trying to break up but too scared to say the words. In sales, one usually treats potential customers with kindness because they hope for return business or referrals. It seems BHG has enough customers, so they do not need to concern themselves with image. This means you are all encouraged to seek a lender who has the professionalism and savvy required to manage money (and people). At least I will be working with a more professional lender now, so thank you BHG for sparing me from an unhappy relationship with your company.",

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "IF I COULD GIVE A LOWER SCORE I WOULD",
      "text": "Applied and was approved for a BHG Financial Business credit card on 11/27/22 after they ran a credit check to verify my credit scores and identity.\nCredit limit $10000\nReceived physical card in mail on 12/20/22.\nWent to activate card same day on BHG card activation website and received message saying they could not activate card \"due to fraud concerns\".\nFurther prompts said to call customer service to resolve.\nI called and was told to send in front and back of drivers license and a copy of utility bill with same address which I immediately did by email on12/20/23.\nOver the course of the next 33 days I tried activating the credit card numerous times since I had sent in the proper verification.\nNo success.\nI called the customer service several times and each time they had to ask me the card number, my social security number, birthdate, email, and card expiration number just to continue ( just pointing out that they were were positive I wasn't fraudulent when making inquiries and let me proceed with call).\nEach call resulted with customer service stating they had my documentation and it had to make it's way through the back office.\nTold to be patient and keep trying to activate card because they were busy.\nI probably tried activating 20 times over the course of 33 days.\nI probably called 10 times and received same answers to keep trying.\nOn 1/24/23 I received email stating account was closed and if I didn't request that to call in.\nI did so and was told my verification for fraud wasn't approved.\nI asked how is that possible?\nBHG asked for front and back of drivers license and utility bill with same address which I sent....it wasn't ambiguous.\nCustomer service representative told me there was no way to reopen account now.\nApparently this same thing is happening to almost everyone who opened a BHG Business credit card in the months of Nov/December of 2022. I am on a credit website and people are reporting this same issues with same process.\n\nEdit: Look at the reply from BHG below.\n\nSuch nonsense.\nYou APPROVED my application AND sent me a physical card !!\nWhat the heck does 'after a thorough review your application did not meet our requirements....\" BS mean ???\nThis all happened well after the application stage.\n\nA total dodge and fabrication that doesn't even make any sense.\nAnd apparently BHG did this to hundreds of other small business owners if you read any credit sites.\nApproved application, sent cards out, and then cancelled them after weeks of trying to activate.\nIt would be better to just be more forthcoming and admit the new credit card rollout was botched instead of blaming it on the consumer.\nIt was totally a BHG failure and the company looks like a sleazy lending outfit because of it.",

      "title": "Professionalism upfront but Dismissive and Inconsiderate on the end",
      "text": "BHG initially was wonderful and seemed very professional during the initial process of loan servicing. However please be aware that after that point, this is no longer the case. Yes, those are the ones I’m talking about.\n\nAfter the customer service debacle, I reached out to them and immediately realized it was a bad idea, simply from their tone. It was clear that I was bothering them but one actually said he would get additional information and follow up with me-two days ago. So I reached out today to follow up and immediately received an email to “call customer service”. So in other words-don’t call or reach out to me again.\n\nAs a client, it’s disheartening but I’m sure I’m not the first person this has happened to. So, just be aware that the outpouring of kindness and professionalism on the front end, is certainly not something you should expect on the back end.     {
      "stars": 4,
      "title": "My Experience with BHG Money",
      "text": "I almost never write reviews about anything, but I know how important or life changing getting a loan can be, and if you are browsing here, it means you are considering BHG Money for a loan.\nQuick background, i have a good salary, about 140K and good credit 730ish but due to bad money management from my younger years i ended up with ton of debts and sadly even with my good salary, i was living paycheck to paycheck. After a long debate, I decided a personal loan is the best option for me. This would then enable me to save at least 1,500 a month.\n\nI gotta say like my others here, I was somewhat skeptical based on the negative reviews on here but in the end, I decided \"desperate times call for desperate measures.\" Based on reviews here, the most common negative one was the amount of spams people get, i decided that was not a deal breaker for because i can just ignore them. Another was about prepayment penalty, i can confirm mine does not have any prepayment penalty. Another one was that people got their loan denied late in the process for no apparent reason. This one worried me a little but in the end i decided it was worth a try.\n\nMy experience with BHG Money and various reps were mostly great. They were able to really work with me with a personalized loan, unlike some other lenders who will get you a fixed term based on your credit with not many ways to customized it. BHG was able to modify the loan amount, rate and length based on my needs.\nEvery one of the 3 reps I got in contact with were professional and helpful and provided quick responses.\nPart of my loan term was for BHG to mail out some checks directly to my lenders, i can confirm they were all mailed out and processed correctly.\n\nThe biggest negative feedback I have is that my process took too long from the first day i spoke to the sales rep to funding. It took about 3 weeks. And my funding day was pushed back by a week without really any explanation. So, if you have an emergency and need money within 24-72hrs, BHG may not be your best option.\nAnother feedback that i have which honestly isn't a big deal is that they don't seem to have a portal where you can log in to manage your loan, check upcoming payments, check remaining balance, update automatic withdrawal account etc... it's somewhat disappointing that they don't have such portal in 2022, but again not a dealbreaker.\n\nIn the end my experience with BHG was really good and I would recommend to friends or family. They were able to offer me a personal loan with great terms. I only wish the process was a little faster.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2022-11-05T18:32:14.000Z",
        "experience": ""
      },
      "metadata": {
        "verified": false,
        "useful_votes": 0,
        "page_number": 104,
        "source_url": "https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bhgfinancial.com?page=104"
      }
    },

    {
      "stars": 4,
      "title": "BHG is a very solid lender to consider",
      "text": "I had done my homework and researched BHG and also some of the reviews listed here on Trusted Pilot. So after several direct mail items, I went into the pursuit with my guard up. After seeing multiple good reviews associated with the particular people, Kaylie Beech and Ben Boulos, I reached out to them both directly via LinkedIn. Both followed up immediately and I got a call setup with Kaylie to start the process.\n\nWe talked to my initial concerns credit reporting, background inquiry, accrued interest with pre-payment, and application process. That all was confirmed and checked out and we proceed to the loan application(soft inquiry only) to see what my options would be based off my request loan amount.\n\nThey came back with a really solid option and the communication was really good. After reviewing the offer with Ben, the only reason I didn't pursue the offer was because I had a better presented from another vendor and they also had an online portal to manage the loan. Those were to two main factors that kept me from executing with BHG. This was a unsecured personal loan and the interest was competitive as well as the term flexibility. But again the option was the best for me at this time.\n\nSo amidst all negative reviews, my experience with BHG was a very good one even though we didn't execute a loan. I would recommend them to others as different people have different situations and I believe BHG can be a viable lender. Thanks Kaylie & Ben!",

      "text": "I’m sorry to see that your company promises so much but delivers nothing. What good is it to offer a debt consolidation loan and then be unwilling to help someone consolidate their debt? I have never been delinquent on any unsecured debt in my life. With the loan I applied for, I could have paid off all of my debt and then seen my credit score soar to near 800. Now I have had an inquiry made that will negatively affect my credit score. It is also disappointing that the denial was absolute. No alternative amount was offered. I would have been willing to have BHG pay my creditors directly and close the accounts so there would be certainty that the accounts were paid off.     {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Be very careful",
      "text": "Will never reach out to or do business with BHG Financial again. I asked during the application process what the pre payment fee would be and they would not go into details. If you do not have the money for a project - don’t risk it by getting the money from BHG Financial. BBB accredited somehow but truly more of a legal version of a loan shark. They add on about 14% of fees on top of your personal loan, and depending on your loan term length, you will be locked in to half that loan term length first, before you can pay off the remainder without any pre-payment penalty fees. The pre payment penalty fee is the loan over the full loan term length with all interest - meaning if you were to pay the loan early - you would pay the loan + fees + all interest that would have accrued over the length of the loan. A simple $55k loan will now cost me $100k minimum to pay back. I cannot believe this is legal.",

      "title": "My new go-to lender",
      "text": "For those of you on the fence on getting a loan with BHG, trust me I was there too.     {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "Worst Financial transaction I have ever had.",
      "text": "This has got to be one of the worst transactions that I have ever had from a financial institution. The salesman was hard sell. Not just a courteous follow up. When funded, they sent a check via UPS to an address I listed, but that is not physically deliverable to. 4 days later UPS notified me of a missed delivery that was going to be returned. There Hub for me to pickup was 10 miles away. I was of the understanding that a check would be sent directly to my creditors to payoff the debt. Why else would you ask for detailed payoff amounts and addresses if you were not going to accomplish this? Mind you, the interest clock has already begun, on the day BHG put the check in the mail. Now I have to pay each creditor, but I have no printed checks, who does anymore? So, I have to pay for money orders, and mail the payoff amounts out. This is an additional day and interest is ticking. 10 days have passed since BHG issued the check.\n\nBest part is coming. BHG asked for bank account verification, which I provided. They did not say that this account would be the one to withdraw funds for repayment of the loan. So in 20 days they they tried an ACH from an account that was not intended to have money for withdrawal. It failed, Upon finding this out, I promptly provided the correct account for them to use. You can only telephone this information and follow up with a paper authorization to change this. More days past. The website is useless. Now they have put a collections agency on me for the first missed payment, that was their fault. They have no communication. They did not notify me of a delinquency in any communication form, no text, email, letter, or call. Just the collection agency text and call.\n\nI would never recommend or do business with this organization again!!!!!!!!!",
      "company_response": "",

        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null

    {
      "stars": 1,
      "title": "\"Approved\" then DENIED by info THIEVES, LIARS, and pro SCAMMERS",
      "text": "I was asked to sign a 8821 form to release 2 years of tax return transcripts, as part of the application process, and send over a w-2 for 2021's income, + my very last paystub.\n\nI was then told I was approved, 'scheduled' a call with a \"finance manager\" who told me I was \"approved up to $57,000, but if i chose $52,000 they wouldn't have to overnight me a check to pay off my credit card.\"\n\nSo, simply because I figured choosing $52k or less would have made the process a little bit quicker and easier, I chose $52,000. This occurred during a weekday before Easter weekend but whether it was Wed, Thurs or Fri, I don't recall.\n\nWith the same \"finance manager\" I also had to verify myself via FACIAL BIOMETRIC DATA with my phone, AND sent a bank statement/Void check.\n\nI did all that & was told everything's looking perfect! And \"they will send out the ACH on the following Thursday!!\"\n\nABSOLUTE B.S. He called me Monday, telling me I was DENIED, with no explanation whatsoever, and just that \"Decisions for approval are subject to change at any time after approval\" which really seemed strange to me, but immediately just crushed me, entirely. I felt and still feel, so defeated. Especially since after not hearing anything for many days, I HAD ASSUMED THINGS ARE ON TRACK, and made the foolish mistake of planning certain important things around this, which was, what I thought, an incoming Loan.\n\nSo I called back many times, asking WTH is going on, and as soon as I got the SAME EXACT WORDING, but with robotic like reading, I figured it was a script, or was written in the notes for every representative to use as a response to any calls I may later make, to inquire about my situation. \"Approvals are subject to change blah blah blah\" I also can now see, after reading reviews, that this is CLEARLY COMMON-PRACTICE!!\n\nAfter calling and realizing this must be regular practice, I went back, and looked over my emails with a couple of reps, and found the 8821 that was signed, re-read the email, and saw the rep CLEARLY EMPHASIZED that this was strictly for BHG to \"get 2 years of tax information for your income\" But after opening the document again, I see it was for THE PAST 10 YEARS !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!\n\nINCLUDING GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS AND REMEDIES OR RECOURSE AGAINST BHG IN PERPETUITY!!!!!!!?????????\n\nWHAT the ACTUAL EFF!!!!!!!!!!!!!\n\nWhat an absolute shame. it's just outright ABUSIVE, and I'm sure those who have experienced this as well, know exactly what I mean when I say this is ABSOLUTELY ABUSIVE. It's clearly very deeply entrenched in the procedural ways of doing things at BHG.\n\nHow can they have no remorse towards their fellow Americans.\n\nI'm just in absolute shock, and at a complete loss for words, even now being 5 days after the denial call. I'm seriously left speechless. I am still in disbelief. I can't believe I signed my life over, and gave them the past 10 years of my life, and my facial recognition biometric data, only for them to FOOL ME. This just REALLY, and COMPLETELY shattered my confidence in ANY sort of dealing with financial institutions.\n\nSuch shallow practices and 100% INTENTIONALLY incorrect misinformation that is provided to us, to then mislead and deceive all of us, is criminal. It is just purely reprehensible.\n\nI think that lifting the spirits of any person, ONLY to crush them later, is a way to make sure that you really destroy that person. It is SOOOO much more PAINFUL than to just be denied straight up, and honestly rejected. This is seriously criminal in my eyes.\n\nSTAY AWAY. PLEASE !!!!!!!\n\nGod bless all of you, and I truly hope that more people are able to see this, and less people end up getting emotionally, and spiritually destroyed.",
      "company_response": "",
      "reviewer": {
        "name": "Anonymous",
        "location": "",
        "reviews_count": null
      },
      "date": {
        "published": "2022-04-22T11:23:36.000Z",
        "experience": ""

    {
      "stars": 5,
      "title": "Worth Every Penny",
      "text": "I'm not someone who generally writes reviews, and ignored the request when the loan first funded, but here I am now to give thanks. Really. I'm a high earning attorney - partner at a large law firm. At the inception of my career, however, when I did not earn as much, and had a ton of student loans (for both my wife and me), I racked up a fair amount of credit card debt and loans as the sole breadwinner for my family of 5, creating a hole out of which I could never dig, no matter how hard I tried. To be clear, nobody was shedding tears for me, but I sat mired in a credit score that couldn't escape the low 700s -- no late payments, etc., but a lot of debt and high credit utilization. The debt load was inescapable. In fact, despite my income, I would receive letters in the mail from secured credit card companies, and would occasionally be rejected for credit or credit increases. Embarrassing. I desperately needed a way out if I wanted to live a life commensurate with my income. Let me be clear. BHG's rates are far from perfect, and both the documentation fee and need for an optional limited personal guarantee (realistically, using a personal life insurance policy to back the loan would take too long, and be too arduous, given that you couldn't use one associated with an employer) are frustrating. And the sell was hilariously over-the-top, like a stockbroker scene in Boiler Room. But there was one factor that could not be beat -- unlike a standard personal loan, THIS LOAN IS NOT REPORTED TO YOUR PERSONAL CREDIT PROFILE. Bam. Exactly what I needed. This factor cannot be highlighted or lauded enough. I negotiated as hard as I could, and ultimately took $200K on an 84 month term with no payments in the first 3 months. The funding came almost immediately, and I paid off almost every dime of credit I had racked up over the years. Hopping online paying off every card was utter joy. My credit score skyrocketed almost immediately, and I've been sitting in the 825-835 FICO Score 8 range ever since with zero credit card balance, allowing me -- amongst other things -- to secure an exceptional rate on a jumbo mortgage for a new home I'm building. Never would've happened without BHG. There are a lot of people out there like me. My advice? Go for it. Thanks BHG, for believing in people like me.",

      "stars": 1,
      "title": "The initial contact with BHG told me…",
      "text": "The initial contact with BHG told me that the minimum loan amount was 150k and based on my onboard info I would qualify for the minimum, no prepay penalty and and a potential APR under 10%. Once the underwriter got to my loan request I was told I would qualify for 40k at 17.79 apr with a prepayment penalty if I paid the loan before 48 months. I declined the loan and was then called back with lower rate but no change on the prepayment penalty. Their main self described benefit was that the loan wouldn’t show on my personal or business credit card…the problem with that is that as a business I want to show credit to increase my benefits long term. I accepted the loan because the total interest paid in 48 months is comparable to a personal loan, but the benefit is that I can deduct the interest as a business expense.",
